text: The Song of Songs, [1] which is Solomon's.
W [2] [AA] Let him kiss me with kisses of his mouth,for your love is better than wine, [3]
better than the fragrance of your perfumes. [4]Your name is a flowing perfume—therefore young women love you.
t[AB] Draw me after you! Let us run! [5]The king has brought me to his bed chambers.Let us exult and rejoice in you;let us celebrate your love: it is beyond wine!Rightly do they love you!
W I am black and beautiful,Daughters of Jerusalem [6]—Like the tents of Qedar,like the curtains of Solomon.

Do not stare at me because I am so black, [7]because the sun has burned me.The sons of my mother were angry with me;they charged me with the care of the vineyards:my own vineyard I did not take care of.
W Tell me, you whom my soul loves,where you shepherd, [8] where you give rest at midday.Why should I be like one wanderingafter the flocks of your companions?
M If you do not know,most beautiful among women,Follow the tracks of the flockand pasture your lambs [9]near the shepherds' tents.
M To a mare among Pharaoh's chariotry [10]I compare you, my friend:
Your cheeks lovely in pendants,your neck in jewels.
We will make pendants of gold for you,and ornaments of silver.
W While the king was upon his couch,my spikenard [11] gave forth its fragrance.
My lover [12] is to me a sachet of myrrh;between my breasts he lies.
My lover is to me a cluster of henna [13]from the vineyards of En-gedi.
M [AC] How beautiful you are, my friend,how beautiful! your eyes are doves! [14]
W How beautiful you are, my lover—handsome indeed!Verdant indeed is our couch; [15]
the beams of our house are cedars,our rafters, cypresses.
